blocks.text: The verbs "**носить**", "**возить**" and "**водить**" have basically the same prefixes as the verbs of motion we have studied previously with corresponding changes in meaning. However, many of the prefixed verbs have also secondary meanings, some of which are more important than the basic meanings.

items: В прошлом году я перенёс тяжёлую болезнь.
Я не могу перевести этого слова.
проводить время — to spend the time
В прошлом году здесь провели несколько новых дорог.

blocks.text: Notice also the following expressions: **Прошла неделя**. — A week went by. **Дождь прошёл**. — The rain stopped.

Other meanings from the prefix table: **вы-** — Step out for a short period of time: **Секретарь вышел на десять минут**. — The secretary left for ten minutes. **под-** — **Подвезти** – give someone a lift: **Он подвёз меня до центра**. — He took me (as far as) downtown. **от-** — With transitive verbs, delivering or dropping something off (agent does not remain): **Я отнесу книги в библиотеку**, **потом приду**. — I'll drop the book off at the library, then come. **до-** — Characterizing the duration of a journey, especially when it is long: **Мы наконец доехали до дачи**. — We finally reached the dacha. **пере-** — Changing residence: **Я переехала в другой город**. — I moved to another city. **про-** — Movement beyond one's destination (possibly unintentional): **Я боюсь**, **что мы уже прошли магазин**. — I'm afraid we already passed the store. **на-** — Quantified movement: **Водитель наездил** 50 **километров**. — The driver covered 50 kilometers.

head: verb
Wiktionary's definitions
rows: **провести / проводить**

to lead, to conduct, to guide, to steer, to take; to lay, to construct, to build, to install a road, a pipe, a wire etc.; to carry out, to carry through, to realize, to put into practice, to conduct; to pass over, to run over
**перевести / переводить**

to lead, to convey, to transfer, to move, to shift, to transmit, to switch; to translate, to interpret .mw-parser-output .object-usage-tag{font-style:italic}.mw-parser-output .deprecated{color:var(--wikt-palette-grey-lime-8,olivedrab)}[with с (s, + genitive) ‘from a language’ and на (na, + accusative) ‘into a language’]; to remit (money)
**перенести / переносить**
to transfer, to carry, to transport; (word) to carry over to the next line; to postpone, to put off; to extend
**привести / приводить**
to bring (someone with); to lead (of a road); to result, to lead, to bring; (mathematics) to reduce
**довести / доводить**
to lead, to take, to accompany (to), to bring (into); (cooking) to scald; to drive, to reduce, to bring, to carry
**завести / заводить**
to take, to bring, to lead; to get, to procure, to acquire, to buy; to establish, to set up, to found; to start
**нанести / наносить**
to drift (on); to carry, to waft, to deposit, to wash ashore (e.g. of snow, sand, etc.); to mark (on); to draw (e.g. onto a map); to inflict (on); to cause (to); to bring
**сойти / сходить**
to go down, to come down, to descend, to get off; (figuratively) to come off, to disappear, to go from; to pass by; (figuratively) to pass for, to be taken for
**обойтись / обходиться**

to go around, to bypass (to pass by going around); to walk through, to wander around, to go around, to tour, to go to (many places in an area); to overtake, to outrank, to beat, to outperform (a peer or competitor)
**выйти / выходить**
to exit, to go out; to appear, to be published; to spend, to be used up; to come off, to come out
